title: hotfix: tighten SLO enforcer backoff/order logic to prevent premature regional failover and over-shedding
author: Miguel Santos
description: Fixes a bug in the SLO enforcer where backoff timers and concurrent decision ordering could cause regional failover to trigger prematurely under bursty traffic, resulting in aggressive load shedding and cascading capacity reductions. This PR corrects the backoff multiplier and ordering logic, introduces a lightweight decision-stabilizer that applies hysteresis and prefers local smoothing before cross-region failover, gates debug logs behind a feature flag, and bumps the default rollout config to avoid immediate full deployment. Includes unit and integration tests and a small canary deployment manifest. Tested in canary (us-west-2/us-east-1) with metric-driven watches; observed elimination of spurious failovers and no regression on latency or throughput. Rollout plan: staged canary -> 25% -> 100% with alerts and automatic rollback via config toggle if fail rate or SLO violation increases. Linked Linear: ENG-2481, ENG-2500.
commits: fix(enforcer): correct backoff multiplier and ordering to avoid premature failover
test(enforcer): add unit tests for concurrent decision ordering and backoff edge cases
infra: add canary deployment and feature flag for debug logging
docs(runbook): update SLO enforcer runbook and release notes
release_notes: Hotfix: prevent premature regional failovers and reduce aggressive load shedding by tightening SLO enforcer backoff and ordering logic. Ships guarded by feature flag and staged rollout.
